author: Branko Marcetic
title: According to Polls, Americans Like Socialism a Lot
content: A crop of recent polls shows that socialism’s appeal is surprisingly broad. They also reflect a transformed US political landscape that is ripe for a socialist politician to capitalize on — if they’re willing to step up. title: Forgiveness is Part of Socialism
content: When I tell people I’m interested in the politics of forgiveness, that often surprises them: the idea sounds bad and moralistic. author: Céli Pinto
title: The Most Important Election in Brazilian History
content: We usually say that in general elections, we’re choosing a president, governors and lawmakers for the next four years. That much seems obvious. But in this election, with the first round on October 4 and the runoff on October 25, we’re not just choosing who governs. We’re choosing the country’s future for decades to come. [...]

author: Yanis Varoufakis
title: The Centre-Left’s Slow Suicide
content: “Only dangerous fanatics refuse to compromise,” my mother used to tell me. And so, several decades later, I entered government ready to compromise; a small price to pay, I thought, for delivering a modicum of relief to the suffering majority who had voted us in. Yet the hardest, and the most pertinent, question kept torturing [...]

title: The Power of a Label: How the Word “Terrorist” Kills

author: Christopher Impiglia
title: Revisiting Walter Benjamin as the Midterms Loom
content: As the Left epitomized by the Democratic Socialists of America resurges and Marxist thought returns to the fore, as a real force, not simply as a bogeyman; as the Midterms loom and, through them, we get our first taste of the 2028 Presidential Election, I revisit Walter Benjamin, specifically his Theses on the Philosophy of [...]

author: Yohannes Woldemariam
title: From Tsimdo to Possible Regional War
content: What is happening in Ethiopia is no longer adequately described as another round of the Tigray war. title: Inside the United Nations Tunnel
content: This month, like every year, the United Nations General Assembly takes place. Heads of State take the floor to send messages to the world. These messages are broadcast on TV, transcribed, and recorded in official documents and the press. author: M. Reza Behnam
title: The Mirage of Statecraft: America’s Blind Drift in West Asia
content: For decades, the architecture of West Asia has rested on a comforting fiction: that Pax Americana could indefinitely manage the region through the policy of offshore balancing, security guarantees to autocrats and the supreme might of the U.S. military.  That order is gone.  Not bruised, not bending, but wholly vaporized.  Washington’s illusion that it could [...]

title: Haphazard Luck: Operational Oddities, Terrorist Proxies and RAF Fairford

title: How Do You Build Working-Class Solidarity in Rural America?
content: Confronted as a young adult with his terminal cancer diagnosis, she sorts through a morass of competing values and emotions. author: Phil Wilson
title: Meditation on the Looming Collapse as it Pertains to Resistance
content: Collapse, like many of the terms that we absorb via osmosis, or from niche online sources, has a diffuse, deeply confusing quality. Does it refer to coral reefs, butterflies and moths, nations or ocean circulation? What about the perpetrating factors leading to collapse – what might be understood as being volitional, inadvertent, inevitable or willfully destructive? [...]

content: The New Reality China’s President Xi Jinping’s sixth visit to the US has come and gone.
